info.name: ACI UC4 - New Network on ACI (VLAN, BD, EPG, SVI, L3Out, monitoring) - v1.2
info.description:
**Version 1.2** (2026-10-13)
- L3Out attach now works whatever the VRF or tenant of the L3Out (CSV `l3out`: `NAME`, `TENANT/NAME` or `uni/tn-X/out-Y`; a bare name is looked up in the row tenant, then common, then any tenant)
- Same tenant / common, other VRF: BD relation added + gateway subnets set to `public,shared` (route leaking); pre-flight warns if the contract scope is not tenant/global
- Other tenant: ACI cannot resolve a BD -> L3Out relation across tenants, so it is used as a shared L3Out (subnets `public,shared` + global contract in common or exported); a contract living only in the L3Out tenant is blocked with the fix to apply
- New optional column `l3outCrossVrf` (shared = default, asis = keep `subnetScope`); ambiguous names (same L3Out in several tenants, or common name shadowed by the row tenant) are blocked
- Rollback unchanged: removes only the L3Out relations this collection added (the shared subnets go with the gateway rollback)

**Version 1.1** (2026-10-13)
- New step: attach one or more EXISTING L3Outs to the bridge domain of the CSV row (`l3out` = `L3OUT_A;L3OUT_B`, first one = contract side); already-attached L3Outs left alone, skipped for L2-only BDs; rollback removes only what it added

**Version 1.0** (2026-10-12)
- New network on ACI from the CSV: VLAN + application profile if missing, BD/EPG, existing vPCs (`vpcs`), optional gateway, existing L3Out contract and monitoring policy, optional DHCP relay

# ACI UC4 - New network creation on Cisco ACI (Postman only)

Creates a complete new network on an existing ACI fabric from a CSV (one row = one network/VLAN). Pure APIC REST - no switch other than the APIC is contacted.

| Step | What happens |
|---|---|
| 03.1 VLAN | VLAN added to the VLAN pool of the existing physical domain (`physDom`) **only if missing** |
| 03.2 Application profile | created **only if missing** |
| 03.3 Bridge domain | VRF, `bdUnknownUnicast` (flood/proxy), `bdArpFlood`, GARP EP-move, limit IP learning to subnet |
| 03.4-03.7 EPG | EPG -> BD, physical domain (immediate), static bindings to the **existing vPCs listed in `vpcs`** (+ optional single ports `hostPorts`), trunk / access / access-802.1p |
| 03.8 DHCP relay (optional) | `dhcpRelayPolicy`: label an EXISTING relay policy on the BD; or `dhcpRelayServers` + `dhcpProvider`: one new policy per server. Leave both empty for no DHCP relay |
| 03.9 Gateway | `gatewaySubnets` as ACI anycast gateway (routing on), DHCP labels, L3Out association (`l3out`, `subnetScope=public` to advertise). Leave `gatewaySubnets` empty for an **L2-only** network |
| 03.10 L3Out contract | the EPG provides/consumes the **existing** contract `l3outContract`; the existing L3Out / external EPG is only checked (it is changed only if `l3outAttachContract=true` and its side is missing) |
| 03.11 Monitoring | the **existing** monitoring policy `monPolicy` (tenant or common) is applied to `monApplyTo` |

**Existing objects only:** L3Out, external EPG, contract, monitoring policy and DHCP relay policy (`dhcpRelayPolicy`) must already exist - a missing one stops the run in the pre-flight. The collection never creates or modifies them (except the optional `l3outAttachContract`).

**vPCs:** only the vPC policy groups named in `vpcs` are used; each must already exist and be deployed on the fabric (the leaf pair is read from the APIC). A name that is not an existing vPC stops the run. Per-vPC mode: `VPC-X:access`.

**Safety:** read-only pre-flight with a gate (tenant/VRF, VLAN pool & conflicts, existing BD/EPG, vPC/port existence, AAEP/domain, access-port rules, duplicate subnet in the VRF, L3Out VRF, external EPG + its contract side, contract, monitoring policy, DHCP relay policies / providers), config snapshot, dry-run by default, post-deploy verification, per-row rollback manifest.

**Rollback** (folder 05, `rollbackConfirm=YES`): `rollbackScope=all` (default) removes everything each row created; `cutover` removes only the gateway, L3Out contract and monitoring.

## Environment
`apic`, `apicUser`, `apicPassword`, `apicLoginDomain`, `rollbackConfirm`, `rollbackPreExisting`, `rollbackScope`. Everything else is in the CSV.

## Requirements
- Postman v10.19+ / v11 or Newman 6.1+, SSL verification off for a self-signed APIC certificate.
- Select the **ACI UC4 - New Network (credentials)** environment and the CSV data file in the Collection Runner.

## CLI
```
newman run ACI_UC4_New_Network.postman_collection.json -e ACI_UC4_New_Network.postman_environment.json -d ACI_UC4_New_Network_inputs.csv -k
newman run ... --folder "05 - Rollback (manual)" --env-var rollbackConfirm=YES
```

item.name: 00.2 Resolve the vPCs from the CSV (vpcs column) on the APIC

request.description:
Reads every vPC that actually exists on the APIC (deployed protpaths endpoints), its policy group, AAEP and domains, and decides which vPCs get the static binding. Only vPCs that exist on the APIC are ever used. The AAEP/domain columns are informational - selection does not depend on them.

* `vpcSelection=auto` (default): every existing vPC, filtered by the `vpcInclude` / `vpcExclude` regexes. Policy groups matching `legacyMatch` are tagged as the legacy vPC towards the Nexus pair (bound with `legacyPortMode`).
* `vpcSelection=manual`: uses `vpcPaths`, but drops entries that do not exist on the APIC (with a warning) and fixes pod/node IDs from the APIC when the IPG lives on exactly one vPC pair.

The result is stored in `_vpcPathsEffective` and is what every later step uses.
